result_semantic_payload.summary: Cross-referencing the CRM order table (file:/crm/orders.csv) with the payment processor's settlement log (file:/payments/settlements.log), three settlements are confirmed as CRM orders via a verbatim order-id linkage: ORD-70231 (wangqiang, 20000 USDT, wallet TXabc111), ORD-70232 (zhaolei, 15000 USDT, wallet TXdef222), and ORD-70233 (sunli, 31500 USDT, wallet TXghi333). Amounts agree exactly between the two sources for all three, and all three CRM rows are marked status=paid. The README at file:/README.txt states the linkage rule explicitly: 'Settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim. A settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order.' One settlement entry must therefore stay separate from the CRM orders: the 2024-06-02 line 'settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok', because ORD-72033 does not appear in the CRM table (note the digit transposition vs. ORD-70233). Conversely, the CRM row ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled) has no matching settlement and must remain unmatched on the CRM side. No other log entries exist in the settlement log, so no additional entries require separation.

claim_candidates.text: The linkage between the CRM order table and the payment processor's settlement log is a verbatim order-id match (order_id in orders.csv equals the order= field in settlements.log), as stated in the case README.
Settlement '2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70231 wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000 ok' is confirmed as CRM order ORD-70231 (buyer wangqiang, 20000 USDT, status paid); the amount matches exactly.
Settlement '2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70232 wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000 ok' is confirmed as CRM order ORD-70232 (buyer zhaolei, 15000 USDT, status paid); the amount matches exactly.
Settlement '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-70233 wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500 ok' is confirmed as CRM order ORD-70233 (buyer sunli, 31500 USDT, status paid); the amount matches exactly.

Settlement '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok' must stay separate from the CRM orders: ORD-72033 does not exist in orders.csv, so per the README rule it cannot be treated as the same order as any CRM row.

The unlinked settlement id ORD-72033 is a near-miss digit transposition of the confirmed CRM id ORD-70233 (72033 vs 70233); the amounts also differ (9999 vs 31500), so it is not a variant/typo of the same confirmed order.
limitations: No additional context (e.g., payment-processor raw records or CRM audit log) is available to determine the origin or intent of ORD-72033; it is reported only as an unmatched settlement.
